subject.title: Feature Request: Cron Job Hooks System

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class persisted cron hook lifecycle that can run user-configured shell/webhook/agent actions around scheduled jobs, or should the remaining use cases stay on command cron plus plugin hook surfaces?
rationale: The missing behavior is clear, but the permanent API controls unattended code execution, network calls, config/protocol shape, and overlap with existing command/plugin hooks, so automation should not choose the product/security boundary.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow hook lifecycle
options.body: Approve a scoped pre/post/onError design with explicit permission, timeout, audit, and failure semantics before implementation.

options.title: Plugin API first
options.body: Extend plugin hooks or cron_changed into a safe gate surface before adding per-job core hook fields.

options.title: Keep current surfaces
options.body: Treat command cron plus existing plugin hooks as the supported answer and close or narrow this issue to documentation gaps.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow hook lifecycle
recommendation.body: Approve a scoped pre/post/onError design with explicit permission, timeout, audit, and failure semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already provided the most recent maintainer-style routing on this exact issue and recently touched cron documentation and behavior.
